chunks: From him, from Aḥmad ibn ʿAbdūs, from al-Ḥusayn ibn ʿAlī, from al-Mufaḍḍal ibn Ṣāliḥ, from Layth al-Murādī, from Abī ʿAbdillāh عليه السلام, who said:

I asked him about one afflicted with nosebleed, whose nose continues bleeding from the sun’s decline until the night passes. He said: “He should gesture with his head at the time of every salat (prayer).”
And regarding a man whose bowels have exhausted him, he said: “He should gesture with his head.”

key_terms.إِيمَاءً بِرَأْسِهِ: gesturing with his head for the acts of salat (prayer)
key_terms.اسْتَفْرَغَهُ بَطْنُهُ: his stomach or bowels have weakened and exhausted him through evacuation
key_terms.زَوَالَ الشَّمْسِ: the time of the sun’s decline, i.e. beginning of ẓuhr time
key_terms.يُومِئُ: he indicates or gestures in place of full physical performance

ai.seo_question: How should someone pray if continuous bleeding or bowel illness prevents normal prayer?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling for a person prevented from normal salat (prayer) by continuous nosebleeding or severe bowel evacuation. It instructs such a person to perform the prayer by gesturing with the head, indicating accommodation in worship during a state of ongoing bodily excuse.
